los.text: Describe the process of urinalysis, demonstrating an understanding of the procedures and techniques involved, as informed by pre-reading on CANVAS.
los.html:
1Identity, explain, consent; fresh midstream urine in a clean container (or catheter sample port).
2Gloves, check dipstick expiry and storage.
3Inspect the urine: colour, clarity, smell, blood.
4Dip the strip fully, remove immediately, tap off excess, hold horizontal.
5Read at the stated times against the colour chart (most at 30–60 s; leucocytes at 2 min).
6Dispose of waste, hand hygiene, document results; send MC&S if indicated.

los.text: Perform a simple urine dipstick test and pregnancy test, analyse the results, and interpret the findings, demonstrating the ability to make appropriate clinical inferences based on the outcomes.
los.html:
ResultPossible meaning
Leucocytes + nitritesUTI (nitrites very specific for Gram-negative bacteria)
BloodInfection, stones, cancer, glomerulonephritis, menstruation, rhabdomyolysis (myoglobin)
ProteinKidney disease, pre-eclampsia (in pregnancy), infection
GlucoseDiabetes, pregnancy, SGLT2 inhibitors
KetonesDKA, starvation, vomiting
Bilirubin / urobilinogenObstructive jaundice / haemolysis or liver disease
Specific gravityConcentration (dehydration)
pHStones, infection (Proteus: alkaline)
Pregnancy testUrine hCG cassette; 3 drops in the well, read at 3–5 min (two lines = positive; control line must appear).
CautionDon't dip urine for UTI in over-65s or catheterised patients (asymptomatic bacteriuria is common): diagnose on symptoms.

los.text: Take a focused psychiatric history from a patient, including mood, thought, and perception.
los.html:
SectionContent
Presenting complaintIn their words
MoodLow mood, anhedonia, energy, duration, biological symptoms (sleep, appetite, weight, libido, diurnal variation)
ThoughtHopelessness, guilt, worthlessness; suicidal thoughts and plans
PerceptionHallucinations (voices, visions)
AnxietyWorry, panic, OCD symptoms
Psychiatric historyPrevious episodes, treatment, admissions, self-harm
Drugs and substancesAntidepressants, alcohol, illicit drugs
Personal and social historyChildhood, relationships, work, finances, forensic history
RiskTo self, to others, from others, self-neglect
  • Screening: PHQ-9 (depression), GAD-7 (anxiety).

los.text: Take a history from a non-communicative or minimally talkative patient using appropriate techniques.
los.html:
TechniqueExample
Open, gentle questions with time to answer"How have things been for you lately?"
Tolerate silenceWait; don't rush to fill gaps
Reflect and observe aloud"You seem quite low today"
Empathy and validation"It sounds like things have been really hard"
Simple, short questionsOne at a time
Collateral historyFamily, GP, notes (with consent)
Explore why they're quietLow mood, psychomotor retardation, psychosis, fear, language barrier

los.text: Observe and interpret non-verbal communication cues during patient interactions.
los.html:
CueMay mean
Poor eye contact, slumped postureLow mood, shame
TearfulnessDistress
Restlessness, fidgetingAnxiety, akathisia
Guarded or suspiciousParanoia
Flat or incongruent affectPsychosis, depression
Long pauses, slowed movementPsychomotor retardation (depression)
Self-harm scars, poor self-careRisk, self-neglect
  • Respond: name it gently and explore.

los.text: Assess mental state by observing both objective and subjective features, including appearance, behaviour, and mood
los.html:
Mental state examinationObserve
Appearance and behaviourSelf-care, clothing, eye contact, rapport, psychomotor activity
SpeechRate, volume, tone, quantity
Mood (subjective, their words) and affect (objective)"Low", reactive or flat affect
Thought formFlight of ideas, loosening of associations
Thought contentDelusions, obsessions, suicidal ideation
PerceptionHallucinations
CognitionOrientation, attention, memory
InsightDo they recognise they're unwell?

los.text: Demonstrate the ability to perform a cardiovascular examination with clinical competence, interpret and integrate findings with relevant knowledge to support clinical reasoning, and clearly present these findings to peers or supervisors.
los.html:
• Full routine: see ICM Year 1 › Cardiovascular › LOs 1 and 4.
Competence =
Smooth examination including manoeuvres for murmurs
Interpret and link findings: e.g. AF + pansystolic murmur + basal crackles = mitral regurgitation with heart failure
Present with summary, differential and investigations (ECG, echo, bloods, CXR)

ExplainExample (sertraline)
What it's forTreats depression and anxiety
How to take itOnce daily, with or without food
When it works2–4 weeks, full effect 6–8 weeks
Common side effectsNausea, headache, anxiety at first; usually settle
Important warningsDon't stop suddenly (discontinuation symptoms); seek help if worse or suicidal thoughts (especially under 25)
ReviewFollow-up in 2 weeks (1 week if under 25 or at risk)
  • Check understanding (teach-back) and give written information.
